leaders.notes: Held the titles of chancellor and CEO; resigned October 6, 1997 after a federal investigation found he had misrepresented information on a 1994 U.S. Department of Education grant application, leading to a $345,666 settlement.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President of Church Relations / Dean, Cooper School of Missions and Biblical Studies
leaders.notes: Named interim president after Edwards' resignation in October 1997; had joined the Carey faculty in 1991 after pastoring First Baptist Church of Laurel, MS. Formally elected permanent president in August 1998.
Grew enrollment from about 1,980 to 3,000 students, paid off the college's $7M+ debt, and completed $22M in construction/renovation. Died in office in March 2006 from complications of ALS.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President (previously Dean, School of Psychology and Counseling; VP for Graduate and Off-Campus Programs)
leaders.notes: First William Carey alumnus to serve as its president; named ninth president in April 2007, oversaw creation of the College of Osteopathic Medicine, retired in 2022 after 15 years. Died November 2023.
10th president of William Carey University; internal promotion, took office August 16, 2022, succeeding retiring president Tommy King.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Admissions, Retention and Development (previously department chair, Business and Economics)
leaders.notes: First woman president of William Woods and the university's first internally-promoted president; served a record 31 years (1990-2021), the first presidential change in over three decades.

leaders.nextRole: Resigned to pursue other professional opportunities (specifics not publicly disclosed)
leaders.notes: 13th president; took office October 2021 and was formally inaugurated May 2022 (first WWU inauguration ceremony in 32 years). Announced resignation in December 2024, departing effective January 2025.

leaders.priorTitle: Chair, Board of Trustees (retired UPS executive)
leaders.priorInstitution: William Woods University Board of Trustees
leaders.notes: William Woods alumna and board chair named Acting President on December 13, 2024 after Moreland's abrupt resignation, becoming the first WWU graduate to lead the institution; a national search for a permanent successor was underway as of mid-2026.

leaders.priorTitle: Associate Professor / Executive Director, Title I Elementary and Secondary Education Act program
leaders.notes: First and only female president of Wilmington College/University; grew enrollment past 10,000 students and led the institution for 26 years before retiring in 2005. Later honored in the Hall of Fame of Delaware Women.

3rd president; worked alongside predecessor Doberstein as EVP/Provost for years before succeeding her on July 1, 2005. Oversaw the college's transition to university status and growth past 21,500 students; retired June 30, 2017 after 30 years at the institution.

First African American woman to serve as president of any university in Delaware; joined Wilmington University in 1989 and rose through internal roles before becoming president in July 2017, unanimously approved by the Board of Trustees.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Development (previously VP for Institutional Advancement at Meredith College, 1980-1987)
leaders.notes: Served 23 years, the longest-running college presidency in North Carolina at the time of his May 2015 retirement; later inducted into the NC Sports Hall of Fame and awarded an honorary degree by UNC Pembroke.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice President for Student Life and Enrollment Services (previously associate dean of students, university planning officer, dean of enrollment management)
leaders.notes: 10th president of Wingate University; a two-time Wingate graduate and internal promotion, named March 18, 2015 and took office June 1, 2015, succeeding Jerry McGee.
